adults.title: Softer Hearts, Stronger Links
adults.big_idea: In the house of the Lord, Jesus Christ teaches, heals and unites us, and we answer by building a personal temple culture of sacrifice and gratitude.
adults.objective: Learners will name one spiritual blessing of the temple they want more fully in their lives and choose one element of personal temple culture to act on this week.
prepare: Read Elder Gong's talk, especially paragraphs 3-16 (three doctrinal foundations) and 17-30 (five elements of personal temple culture).
Write on the board: commotion, contention, cares. Leave room beside them for three more words.
Bring paper and pens for everyone, and three slips of paper for the group assignments in segment 2.

Remember that class members' circumstances differ: some live far from a temple, some do not hold a recommend now, some are single or have family members who have made other choices. Teach so that each one feels the Lord's invitation is for them.

segments.name: A place of safety
steps: After the prayer, point to the three words on the board. Ask learners to think silently of where they met one of them this week.
Read key quote 1 (T01.03) aloud. Write safety, harmony, holiness beside the first three words.
Ask the first question below. Take two or three short answers. Welcome answers about preparing for the temple, a temple far away, or a feeling at an open house, as well as answers about attending.
questions: When has the house of the Lord, or preparing to go there, been a place of safety, harmony or holiness for you?

segments.name: Three foundations
steps: Explain that Elder Gong taught three doctrinal foundations before he spoke about what we do. Divide into three groups (at home, take them one at a time).
Group 1 reads paragraphs 6-7 and Moses 1:39. Group 2 reads paragraphs 8 and 11-13 and Alma 34:33. Group 3 reads paragraphs 14-16 and Doctrine and Covenants 132:7.
Give four minutes. Each group prepares one sentence that answers: What does this foundation teach about what the Lord offers us in His house, and what is our part?
Hear each group's sentence, one minute each. Write a few words from each on the board.
After group 3, read Elder Bednar's sentence (aligned quote, T31.17) and ask the question below.
questions: Why is it hopeful that this sealing by the Holy Ghost comes over time, as we repent and honor our covenants, and not all at once?

segments.name: Hearts softened on both sides of the veil
steps: Read paragraph 12 together (key quote 2 is its heart). Invite learners to notice the five short sentences Elder Gong says we exclaim.

Silent writing, two minutes: Ask each person to write, for their eyes only, the name or initials of a family member, living or dead, with whom things have been hard, and one of the five sentences they would like to be able to say.
Do not ask anyone to share what they wrote. Ask the questions below and let those who wish respond in general terms.

Read paragraph 10 and Elder Bednar's promise (aligned quote, T31.28). Testify briefly that the Lord honors agency and that no one who is faithful will in the end lose a promised blessing because of another person's choices.
questions: Why might serving someone in the temple change how we feel about that person?
What does Elder Gong say Jesus Christ can help us do? Which of those three do you most need right now?

segments.name: Five elements of personal temple culture
steps: List the five elements on the board in a few words each: a dedication is a beginning; temple sacrifice in new ways; everything testifies of Jesus Christ; a spirit of gratitude; our own temple clothes.
In pairs, each person chooses the element that speaks to them today and tells their partner why. Three minutes.
Read aloud the exchange about the small temple (paragraphs 25-26; key quote 3). Ask the question below.
Check for understanding: ask two or three people to finish the sentence, Personal temple culture means that I ...
questions: How does the way we speak about a temple, or about the people who serve us there, show what we treasure?

segments.name: Choose and act
steps: Read the invitations from the talk listed in this lesson. Point out the promise in Elder Gong's closing words (key quote 4): God and temple ordinances can protect, bless and inspire, bring forgiveness, healing and peace, and unite loved ones.
Silent writing, two minutes: each person writes one thing they will do this week and when. Offer the ideas under Act this week for anyone who is unsure.
Invite one or two people to share their plan if they wish. Bear a short testimony of the Savior.
Follow up: tell the class you will begin next week by asking what they noticed or felt as they acted. Next week, ask it first.
questions: What is one thing the Lord is inviting you to do, and what blessing do you hope for as you do it?

key_quotes.text: In a world of commotion, contention, and cares, the Lord invites us to a place of spiritual safety, harmony, and holiness—the house of the Lord.
We find hope and healing when we perform temple ordinances for family members with whom we may earlier have had difficult relationships. Jesus Christ can help us mend, forgive, move forward.

ordinances are not big or small. Covenants are not big or small. Please let us never speak of a temple as big or small, elaborate or plain. Let us always only speak with love and gratitude for ‘Holiness to the Lord, the House of the Lord.’
So God and temple ordinances can protect, bless, and inspire; bring forgiveness, healing, and peace; and unite loved ones here and away.

scriptures.use: Group 1 reads it with paragraphs 6-7 and looks for how Elder Gong describes Heavenly Father's work and glory in terms of families.
Group 2 reads it with paragraph 13. Ask what blessing Elder Gong says we delay when we delay repentance.
Group 3 reads it with paragraphs 14-16 and looks for what makes a covenant last beyond this life.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Bednar
aligned_quotes.text: Receiving this ratifying sealing by the Holy Ghost typically is not a one-time event; rather, it comes over time as we repent sincerely and consistently, honor our covenants, and yield our hearts unto God.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Bednar
aligned_quotes.text: No faithful disciple will ultimately be deprived of any eternal blessing God has promised because of another individual’s unrighteous exercise of moral agency.

invitations.text: Please “do not procrastinate the day of your repentance until the end.”
let us celebrate and treasure even more the spiritual blessings temples bring
in the chain of your eternal family, please be a strong link
please consider saving for and buying your own ceremonial temple clothes

takeaways: The house of the Lord is a place of spiritual safety, harmony and holiness, and everything in it testifies of Jesus Christ.
Through temple service the Savior can help me mend, forgive and move forward in my family relationships.
I build my own temple culture through sacrifice, gratitude and honoring my covenants.
act: Set a date this week or this month to worship in the house of the Lord. If a temple is far away or you do not hold a recommend now, take one step toward it: a prayer, a conversation with your bishop, or a savings plan.
Find one family name to take to the temple, or prepare one for someone else to take. If a relationship with that person was hard, pray for a softened heart as you do the work.
For one week, speak of your temple and those who serve there only with love and gratitude. Notice what changes in you.
If you are endowed and it is possible, begin setting aside a little toward your own ceremonial temple clothes, or take reverent care of the ones you have.
adapt: At home: skip the groups. Read paragraphs 11-12 and 25-28 together, do the silent writing, and let each person choose one of the five elements to act on.
Short on time: keep segments 1, 3 and 5. The silent writing in segment 3 and the personal plan in segment 5 matter most.
Large class: have neighbors form the three groups by rows and take only one sentence from each foundation.

youth.title: Be a Strong Link
youth.big_idea: In the house of the Lord, Jesus Christ unites families on both sides of the veil, and I can be a strong link in my eternal family.
youth.objective: Youth will explain in their own words why the temple matters to them now and choose one specific way to be a strong link this week.
prepare: Read Elder Gong's talk. Mark paragraphs 2-4, 12, 25-28 and 32.
Cut about 30 strips of paper (roughly 3 by 20 cm) and bring two rolls of tape or two staplers, plus pens.
Write on the board: Why did the temple workers cross the road?
Ask youth to have scriptures or Gospel Library ready. Phones will be used in segment 5; plan to pair up anyone without one.

Remember that some youth are the only members in their family, or have family situations that are complicated. Elder Gong's own parents were the only members in either of their families. Let that be good news in your class.

segments.name: Riddle and chain race
steps: As youth arrive, point to the riddle on the board and take guesses. Give Elder Gong's first answer: to help the people on the other side. Say that he gave a second answer at the end, and you will come back to it.

Split into two teams. Give each team strips, tape and one pen. They have 90 seconds to build the longest paper chain they can, with a different name written on each link (their own names first, then family members or people they love).

Call time. Measure the chains. Have each team gently pull its chain until it breaks, and notice that one link giving way was enough. Keep it light; the point is the chain, not whose name was on the link.
questions: What decided how strong the whole chain was?

segments.name: A strong link
steps: Read paragraph 28 aloud together. Ask youth to listen for what Elder Gong says about his own father and mother.
Pair-share for two minutes on the first question below. Then take a few answers from the whole class.
Read Elder Morgan's sentence (aligned quote, T13.18). Ask the second question.
Say plainly: wherever you are in your family's story, first link or fifth generation, Elder Gong's invitation is the same (invitation, T01.28).
questions: Elder Gong says some new converts feel alone. What does he tell them, and how could that help someone your age who feels like the only one in their family or school trying to follow the Savior?
If covenants bless more than the person who makes them, who could be blessed by the covenants you keep?

segments.name: Six-word headlines
steps: Ask: Honestly, why does the temple matter to someone who is 13 or 17? Take one or two quick answers without correcting them.
Form three groups. Group 1 reads paragraphs 3-4. Group 2 reads paragraph 6 and Moses 1:39. Group 3 reads paragraphs 11-12.
Each group has three minutes to write a headline of six words or fewer that captures what the Lord does for us in His house, and to choose the one phrase from the paragraph that proves it.
Groups read their headline and their phrase. Let the class vote for the headline they would most want to remember (no voting for your own).
Check for understanding: ask one volunteer to answer the opening question again, using something they just read.
questions: Which of these blessings do you want most right now: safety, family, or healing and forgiveness? Why?

segments.name: Big or small?
steps: Tell the story from paragraphs 25-26 in your own words: someone told Elder Gong they were happy to have a temple but sorry it was small. Read his answer (key quote 2).

Role play in pairs, two minutes. One person plays a friend who says their temple is not as impressive as one in another city, or complains about a long wait at the baptistry. The other answers kindly, using Elder Gong's idea in their own words. Then switch.
Ask one pair to show the class. Then ask the question below.
questions: Elder Gong says attending the temple is a sacred privilege and not an entitlement. What does gratitude look and sound like when you are actually there?

segments.name: Find a link
steps: Read paragraph 22 and ask youth to pick out the three things Elder Gong says we can do now that temples are closer.

Phones out, with a purpose. Each youth (or pair) opens the Family Tree app or FamilySearch and has four minutes to find one ancestor they did not know about and one fact about that person. Anyone without an account or a tree writes two questions they will ask an older relative this week.
Ask two or three youth to introduce the person they found in one sentence.
Read the promise in paragraph 28: when you take family names to the temple, your eternal family extends on both sides of the veil.

segments.name: Choose your link
steps: Return to the riddle. Read Elder Gong's second answer (key quote 3).
Hand each youth one blank strip. They write one thing they will do this week to be a strong link (see Act this week), then take it home or tape it inside their scriptures.
Bear a short testimony that Jesus Christ is the one who unites families. Follow up: tell them you will add a link to the class chain next week for every person who reports back, and do it.

key_quotes.text: Whatever generation you are in the Church, in the chain of your eternal family, please be a strong link.

ordinances are not big or small. Covenants are not big or small. Please let us never speak of a temple as big or small, elaborate or plain. Let us always only speak with love and gratitude for ‘Holiness to the Lord, the House of the Lord.’
So God and temple ordinances can protect, bless, and inspire; bring forgiveness, healing, and peace; and unite loved ones here and away.
In a world of commotion, contention, and cares, the Lord invites us to a place of spiritual safety, harmony, and holiness—the house of the Lord.

scriptures.use: Group 2 reads it with paragraph 6 and tells the class how Elder Gong connects Heavenly Father's work and glory to families.
Optional in segment 2: read it in pairs and look for the power the Prophet Joseph Smith describes. Ask how that power makes the links in a family chain hold.
Use in segment 6 if time allows: read it with paragraph 13 and ask what Elder Gong says the Savior wants us to have now.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Morgan
aligned_quotes.text: They do not bless just the maker of the covenant but are generational in their impact.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Fale
aligned_quotes.text: It is often through families, despite all their imperfections, that our Father teaches us about His love.

invitations.text: in the chain of your eternal family, please be a strong link
Please let us never speak of a temple as big or small, elaborate or plain.
let us always be grateful for the gifts of eternity sacred temples bring

takeaways: The house of the Lord is a place of safety and holiness in a noisy world, and it is for me.
Jesus Christ unites families on both sides of the veil, and I can be a strong link in mine.
Ordinances and covenants are not big or small, so I speak of every temple with love and gratitude.
act: Find one family name this week and make a plan with a parent or leader to take it to the temple.
Ask an older relative two questions about someone in your family you never met, and write down the answers.
If you hold a temple recommend, set a date to go. If you do not yet, talk with your bishop or a parent about one step toward it.
For one week, say only grateful things about your temple and the people who serve there, and say thank you to a temple worker the next time you go.
music: I Love to See the Temple
adapt: At home: make one family chain together, read paragraph 28, and spend the phone time on your own family tree with a parent telling one story about a name you find.
Small class (two or three youth): skip the teams and the vote. Build one chain together and let each youth write a headline for a different paragraph.
Short on time: keep segments 1, 2 and 6, and give segment 5 as the challenge for the week.

children.title: Thank You for the House of the Lord
children.big_idea: The temple is the house of the Lord, and I am thankful for it.
children.objective: Children will say that the temple is the house of the Lord and name one reason they are thankful for it.
prepare: Read paragraphs 3-6 and 25-27 of Elder Gong's talk.
Bring a picture of a temple (from the meetinghouse library, a Church magazine or Gospel Library).
Bring building blocks (or paper cups), a soft ball, paper, crayons and a few strips of paper with tape.
Write on two small pieces of paper: Holiness to the Lord, the House of the Lord.

segments.name: Welcome and sing
steps: Invite a child to pray. Hold up the picture of the temple and ask what it is.
Sing I Love to See the Temple together. Ask the children to point to the picture each time they sing the word temple.
Teach the truth for today and have the children repeat it with you three times, first in a whisper, then in a speaking voice, then with a hand on their heart: The temple is the house of the Lord.

segments.name: Noisy world, peaceful place
steps: Tell the children that Elder Gong, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, said the world can be full of noise and worries. Have everyone stand and march, wiggle and stomp in place for ten seconds.
Say: Freeze. Then say that the Lord invites us to a place that is safe and holy, His house. Have the children tiptoe to the temple picture, fold their arms and stand very still for ten seconds.
Do it twice more. Each time they reach the picture, whisper together: The temple is the house of the Lord.
Sit down and ask the questions below.
questions: How did you feel when everything was noisy? How did you feel when we were still?
Where do you feel peaceful and close to Jesus?

segments.name: Big temple, small temple
steps: Make two groups. One group builds a big temple with many blocks. The other builds a small temple with only a few. Give them two minutes.

Tell the story simply: Someone once told Elder Gong they were happy to have a temple but sorry it was a small one. Elder Gong lovingly taught that the sacred things we do in the temple are not big or small. He asked us to always speak about every temple with love and thanks.
Let a child place one of the paper signs on each block temple. Read the sign aloud.
Ask the questions below. Then have everyone point to each temple in turn and say: The temple is the house of the Lord.
questions: Which one of these is the house of the Lord?
What kind words can we say about the temple?

segments.name: A chain of love
steps: Tell the children that in the temple Heavenly Father teaches us His plan of happiness and blesses us. His work is to help us come back to Him with our families, happy and forever.
Give each child a strip of paper. Ask them to draw the face of someone they love on it. Any person they love is a good choice.
Tape the strips into one chain, one child at a time. As each link is added, the class says: Thank you for the temple.
Hold up the finished chain. Say that Elder Gong asked each of us to be a strong link, and that Jesus helps us stay close to the people we love.

segments.name: Draw and tell
steps: Give each child paper and crayons. Ask them to draw a temple and to draw themselves beside it.
While they draw, hum or softly sing I Love to See the Temple again.
Walk around and ask each child the question below. Write their answer at the bottom of their picture, or let older children write it themselves.
Invite two or three children to show their picture and tell the class their answer.
questions: What is one reason you are thankful for the temple?

segments.name: Roll, say and choose
steps: Sit in a circle. Roll the ball to a child. That child says The temple is the house of the Lord, or says one thing they are thankful for about the temple, then rolls the ball to someone else. Continue until everyone has had a turn.
Remind the children that each of them is a child of God and He loves them. The temple is one of the places where He blesses us.
Invite each child to choose one thing to do this week: thank Heavenly Father for the temple in a prayer, or show their picture to someone at home and tell them what the temple is.
Tell them you will ask next week who said thank you for the temple. Next week, ask before anything else. Close with a prayer by a child, and help them thank Heavenly Father for the temple.

key_quotes.text: the Lord invites us to a place of spiritual safety, harmony, and holiness—the house of the Lord.
Let us always only speak with love and gratitude for ‘Holiness to the Lord, the House of the Lord.’
Heavenly Father’s work and glory is for us to return to Him, united as families, happy and forever.

scriptures.use: In the chain segment, read it aloud (or have an older child read it). Explain in simple words, as Elder Gong did, that Heavenly Father's work is to help us return to Him with our families.
Before the opening song, tell the children that Elder Gong reminded us that before we came to earth there was singing for joy about Heavenly Father's plan. Today we sing for joy about the temple.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Fale
aligned_quotes.text: I am a child of God and He loves me.

invitations.text: let us always be grateful for the gifts of eternity sacred temples bring
Please let us never speak of a temple as big or small, elaborate or plain.

takeaways: The temple is the house of the Lord.
Every temple is holy, whether it is big or small.
I can say thank you to Heavenly Father for the temple.
act: Thank Heavenly Father for the temple in a prayer this week.
Put your temple picture where you will see it and tell someone at home: The temple is the house of the Lord.
When you see a temple or a picture of one, say something kind and thankful about it.
music: I Love to See the Temple
I Am a Child of God

adapt.younger: For ages 3-7: shorten the story to two sentences and let the blocks do the teaching. Repeat the truth after every activity and add an action (hands together like a roof). Give helpers jobs: holding the picture, placing the signs, carrying the chain. In Draw and tell, give them a simple temple outline you have sketched and let them color it and add themselves.
adapt.older: For ages 8-11: have a child read Moses 1:39 aloud and another read key quote 2 from Elder Gong. Ask a harder question: Why do you think Elder Gong said the sacred things done in the temple are not big or small? Let an older child lead the noisy and peaceful game and run the ball review. In Draw and tell, have them write one sentence of thanks to Heavenly Father under their picture.
